transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess... people at work have been saying I’m hard to follow. When I try to explain inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, my words sort of jump around—trucks, Thursdays, the church grill, my boss’s tone—and then everyone just looks at me like they don’t know what I’m talking about.
Do you have days where your words don't jump around like that?

I mean... probably, yeah. Some days it’s not as bad. But when I’m trying to explain the inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, it can start jumping around again, and then people just sort of stare at me.
Do you feel like your thoughts are connected and make sense when you're talking, even if others don't understand you?

To me it feels connected at the time, I think. Like the inventory thing leads to the trucks, then Thursday, then… the church grill somehow. But when I say it out loud, people look like they can’t follow it. So maybe it makes sense in my head more than it does coming out.
Does your speech jump around like that when you're talking about things outside of work, like hobbies or what you did over the weekend?

Sometimes, yeah. Not just work. If I’m talking about the weekend, it can go from trucks to Thursday to that church grill thing… then my boss’s tone, even if that’s not what I meant to talk about. People don’t really follow it.
Do you feel upset or anxious when people don't understand what you're trying to say?
Yeah… I guess a little. Mostly I just get quiet. It’s frustrating, but I don’t always want to get into it.
Do you ever think that things are happening or that people are out to get you in a way that doesn't seem real to others?
I don’t know… I mean, I don’t think so. Sometimes things feel off, but I’m not sure I’d say people are out to get me.
Do you ever think that things are happening in a way that doesn't seem real to others?
I’m not sure what you mean exactly. Sometimes things feel strange, like… off somehow, but I don’t know if that’s what you’re asking. I usually just keep it to myself.
Do you ever feel like things you see or hear on the TV, radio, or in newspapers are specifically about you?
Not really… I don’t think so. I mean, sometimes something catches my attention, but I don’t usually think it’s about me specifically.
Do you ever hear voices or sounds that other people can't hear?
No… I don’t think so. Sometimes I hear little noises around the house, but nothing I’d say was… voices or anything like that.
Do you find your speech jumping around like that when you're talking to family or close friends, not just at work?

Yeah… sometimes. Not just at work. If I’m talking to family, I’ll start trying to explain something simple and it kind of jumps around—like from the schedule to the delivery trucks to… something about church, or my boss’s tone. Then they look at me like I lost them.
Do you find it hard to organize your thoughts when you're not talking to someone, like when you're writing or thinking to yourself?

Yeah… sometimes. Even if I’m just thinking it through, or trying to write down the inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, it doesn’t stay in order. It’ll go from the trucks to Thursday to… something at church, or my boss’s tone, and then I’m not sure how I got there.
Do you have times when your thoughts feel completely organized and your speech doesn't jump around at all?

Sometimes, yeah… I think there are times I’m fine. But when I’m trying to explain the inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, it can start jumping around—trucks, Thursday, the church grill, my boss’s tone—and then people just look at me like they can’t follow.
Has your speech been jumping around like that for as long as you can remember, or is it something that started happening more recently?
More recent, I guess. It wasn’t always like this. People started noticing the jumbled explanations and me stopping oddly on the sales floor maybe… six months ago.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are being controlled or influenced by something outside of yourself?
I don’t know… controlled, I’m not sure I’d put it that way. Sometimes my thoughts just don’t feel like they line up right, but I haven’t really thought of it as something outside doing it.
Do you have any beliefs that are not based on reality, such as thinking you have special powers or that you're in danger when you're not?
I don’t think so. I mean… special powers, no. Danger… not really like that. I get uneasy sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I believe something like that.
Do you have times when this jumping around of your thoughts and speech happens more frequently or intensely than at other times?

Yeah… more at work, I think. When I’m trying to explain inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, it can get worse. I’ll start on the trucks, then somehow I’m talking about Thursday, or the church grill, or my boss’s tone, and people just… look at me like they lost what I was saying.
Do you have times when your thoughts and speech are completely normal and don't jump around at all?

Sometimes, sure. If it’s simple, I’m okay. But when I have to explain the inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, that’s when it starts slipping around… trucks, Thursday, the church grill, my boss’s tone. Then people look at me like they can’t follow.
Do you have periods of time where this jumping around of your thoughts and speech stops completely?

Not completely, no… I mean, it’s better when I’m not explaining things. But it’s why I came in, really—when I try to go over inventory or the weekend schedule, my words start going off… trucks, Thursday, the church grill, my boss’s tone. People don’t seem to follow me.
Does this jumping around of your thoughts and speech happen all the time, or are there times when it stops for a while?

It’s not every second, no. It eases up when I’m not having to explain much. But when I try to go over inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, that’s when my words start jumping around… trucks, Thursdays, the church grill, my boss’s tone. People look like they can’t follow me.
Has this issue with your thoughts and speech jumping around affected your relationships or job performance in a significant way?

Yeah… it has. Work mostly. They don’t really trust me to run the busy weekend shifts anymore, and after my review my boss said I could be suspended if I don’t get it together.

At home… my wife’s had to take over some things I used to handle. People were getting confused, or uncomfortable, I guess. So… yes, it’s affected things.
